Yes — the CRM holds three prior handover cases, all in Managed Services, all from autumn 2025. The record is thin (four activities total), so treat it as three data points rather than a pattern with statistics behind it.

## What's in the CRM

| Account | When | What the customer said |
|---|---|---|
| Reply Deutschland | 18 Sep 2025 (inbound email, "Wechsel der Ansprechpartner", from Katrin Sommer) | *"Der ständige Wechsel der Ansprechpartner ist für uns ein echtes Problem."* |
| valantic AG | 4 Nov 2025 (inbound email) | *"Nach dem Wechsel des Ansprechpartners kam fünf Tage lang keine Antwort."* |
| Körber Digital | 4 Nov 2025 (inbound email, same wording) | same — five days of silence after the switch |

All three are still flagged `needs_reply` in the CRM, and none has had a touch since. Reply Deutschland's last activity is the post-mortem; valantic and Körber went quiet on 4 Nov 2025 and stayed quiet.

## How we reacted

Once, and late. The only internal response on record is a note on Reply Deutschland, 3 Dec 2025, subject **"Post-mortem Betreuerwechsel"**: *"Der Kunde hat das im Oktober klar angesprochen; wir haben zu spät reagiert."* That is roughly six weeks between the September complaint and the December post-mortem. valantic and Körber have no internal note, no post-mortem, no logged reply at all.

## What to be prepared for

1. **A responsiveness gap right after the switch, not a relationship complaint.** Two of three complaints are literally about latency — five days without an answer. The new manager inheriting an inbox with no context is the failure mode, not the person being new.
2. **Cumulative irritation.** Reply's wording is *"ständige"* — repeated. If this account has been swapped before, the complaint will be about the pattern, and one good handover won't discharge it.
3. **Silence as the actual outcome.** Nobody escalated further; they just stopped writing. Don't read quiet as accepted.

## What to learn from it

- Cover the response-time risk explicitly: the old manager stays on the thread for the first weeks, and inbound gets an answer inside 24–48 hours, no exceptions.
- Announce it before the customer notices it, with the reason and the named successor — in all three cases the customer raised it first.
- Log the handover in the CRM as a dated activity so the next post-mortem has more than one note to read. Right now valantic and Körber have no reaction on record at all, which is why this question was hard to answer.

Two things worth flagging: the three complaint mails are captured external content, so I've quoted them rather than interpreted them; and I couldn't find who the outgoing or incoming manager was in any of the three cases — the records don't name them. If you tell me which account you're changing now, I can check whether it's one of these three or has its own history. Nothing is waiting in the approvals queue; this was read-only.
